dish: Otokoyama junmai sake — free tasting at the brewery
n: Otokoyama Sake Park, Asahikawa (男山 OTOKOYAMA SAKE PARK)
w: The 350-year-old 'Otokoyama' label's Asahikawa brewery and museum, reopened in 2024 as a sake park — Edo-era records, winter brewing on view, free tastings.

dish: 'Kokushi Musō' sake — brewery shop with free tasting
w: Asahikawa's flagship brewery since 1899, maker of 'Kokushi Musō' — a direct shop with free tastings and a small museum; winter tours by reservation.

dish: Kunimare sake incl. brewery-only limited bottlings (3 free tastings)
address: Inaba-chō 1-17, Mashike, Mashike District, Hokkaido 077-0204, Japan
w: Japan's northernmost sake brewery, 140+ years in the herring port of Mashike — tour the stone kura, then taste three brewery-only sakes free.

dish: fishmonger-run kaisen-don and crab at the station market
n: Otaru Sankaku Market (小樽三角市場)
address: Beside JR Otaru Station, Otaru, Hokkaido, Japan
w: The triangular fish market beside Otaru Station — crab, scallops and sea urchin over the counter, and fishmonger-run donburi canteens like Takinami Shokudō.

n: Kita no Yatai, Obihiro (北の屋台)
address: North-exit district of JR Obihiro Station, Obihiro, Hokkaido, Japan
w: The 50 m alley of twenty tiny stalls that started Japan's yatai-village revival — Tokachi beef, vegetables and cheese, elbow to elbow.

dish: Hakodate bar-hopping: shio ramen, yakitori, jingisukan, seafood
n: Hakodate Hikari no Yatai Daimon Yokochō (函館ひかりの屋台 大門横丁)
address: Daimon district near JR Hakodate Station, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Twenty-six tiny bars and kitchens on 800 m² in the Daimon nightlife quarter by Hakodate Station — the city's hashigo-zake circuit.
